chunks: Al-Saffar from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qassani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man from the people of war (non-Muslims) who converts to Islam in the land of war, and the Muslims gain dominance over them afterwards. He said: 'His Islam is Islam for his own self and for his young children, and they are free, and his wealth, belongings, and slaves are his. As for the adult children, they are booty (fay') for the Muslims, unless they had converted before that. As for the houses and lands, they are booty and do not belong to him, because the land is a land of tribute (jizyah) upon which the rule of the people of Islam has not yet been established, and it is not like what we mentioned, because that (wealth/slaves) can be acquired and taken out to the land of Islam.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ اَلْحَرْبِ: People of war (non-Muslims in non-Muslim lands)
key_terms.فَيْ ءٌ: Booty/Gains (property acquired without battle, typically land)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the land and adult children of a non-Muslim who converts to Islam in a conquered territory?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Fay'* (booty) by distinguishing between movable assets, which remain with the convert, and immovable land, which becomes public property since it was not fully under Islamic jurisdiction prior to conquest. It further establishes that adult offspring are considered part of the spoils unless they converted independently, while children and slaves remain with the father, reflecting the practical realities of early Islamic expansion and the integration of new territories.
